text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- The largest listed Norwegian companies have disappointed the market with their nine-months result. Norsk Hydro, Elkem and Dyno all presented weaker results than analysts had expected. A decrease in raw materials, high prices on electricity in Norway and a weak growth in the world economy are the main reasons.
- Tromsoe beat Bodoe/Glimt 2-1 in the cupfinal on Sunday. Sigurd Rushfelt, Tromsoe scored the decisive goal on overtime.

- Palestinian president Yassir Arafat will visit Norway on Monday. According to Aftenposten, American authorities tried to pursuade Arafat to stay at home and seek to sign an agreement with the Israelis on issues regarding Hebron.
- Egil Haugland, director at Haukeland hospital in Bergen, western Norway, says Norway should export hospital services to wealthy Arabs, Asians and East Europeans.
- In a recent report broker house Fondsfinans recommends to buy shares in Norwegian airline Braathens SAFE. Fondsfinans sees a growth potential of 22 percent for shares in Braathens.
